+  Locked*() implementation notes:
+  - FPC RTL InterlockedXXX() are plain LDXR/STXR loops on AARCH64, with no
+    memory barrier, whereas Locked*() are expected to be full barriers, as the
+    LOCK prefix on Intel - otherwise TLightLock/TRWLock & co don't protect data
+  - so we use LDXR/STLXR loops followed by DMB ISH, which is how the Linux

+  - "dmb #11" is "dmb ish" - FPC 3.2 assembler does not know the ish operand

+.LLockedInc32Loop:
+  ldxr  w1, [x0]
+  add   w1, w1, #1
+  stlxr w2, w1, [x0]
+  cbnz  w2, .LLockedInc32Loop
+  dmb   #11

commits.subject: core: Locked*() are now full memory barriers on FPC non-Intel CPUs
commits.body:
FPC RTL InterlockedCompareExchange/InterlockedExchangeAdd/InterlockedIncrement
are plain LDXR/STXR loops (or LSE CAS/LDADD without acquire/release suffix) on
AARCH64, with no DMB. So TLightLock, TRWLightLock, TRWLock, TMultiLightLock and
the futex-based TOSLightLock only ensure mutual exclusion of the lock word:
stores done inside the critical section may become visible after the UnLock,
and loads may be satisfied before the Lock - which breaks any data protected
by those locks on ARM.

Measured on a RK3588 (Cortex-A76/A55) with FPC 3.2.3, without this commit:
- 4 threads doing "Lock; inc(PlainInteger); UnLock" with TLightLock lose
  about 1-2% of the increments on every run (on the A76 cores)
- TSynThreadPool.Push() returns true but some contexts are never executed
- TSynBackgroundTimer.EnQueue() loses messages, and eventually GPF with a
  corrupted heap when several threads enqueue at the same time

This commit defines FPC_WEAKATOMICS for FPC on non-Intel CPUs, so that all
Locked*() functions are full barriers, as the LOCK prefix on Intel:
- on AARCH64, they are implemented in the new mormot.core.base.asmaarch64.inc
  as LDXR/STLXR loops followed by DMB ISH, which is how the Linux kernel
  implements its "fully ordered" atomics on arm64: an uncontended TLightLock
  Lock/UnLock pair costs 25.5ns on a Cortex-A76 (17.5ns before, but unsafe,
  27.2ns for a pthread mutex) and is unchanged on a Cortex-A55 (26.5ns)
- on other CPUs (e.g. 32-bit ARM), the RTL call is surrounded by a new
  LockedBarrier procedure, i.e. ReadWriteBarrier = DMB ISH; LockedBarrier is
  not inlined, to avoid "ReadWriteBarrier is not inlined" notes
- TOSRWLightLock.ReadUnLock calls the RTL InterlockedDecrement() directly, so
  it gets its own LockedBarrier
commits.author: zen010101
